name: Bodega Catena Zapata Malbec Argentino 2018
text:
## Bodega Catena Zapata Malbec Argentino 2018

**The story.** Catena Zapata, founded in 1902, is the story of modern Argentine wine. The family is known for its pioneering role in resurrecting [Malbec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malbec) and for discovering extreme high-altitude vineyard sites in the Andean foothills of [Mendoza](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Bodega+Catena+Zapata,+Agrelo,+Mendoza,+Argentina&t=k); its Adrianna Vineyard, at almost 5,000 feet, has been called "the Grand Cru of South America" ([Catena Zapata](https://catenazapata.com/family)). Nicola Catena bought his first Mendoza vineyard in 1902; his grandson Nicolás Catena Zapata, inspired by Bordeaux and Napa, was the first to bring Old World winemaking sensibilities to Mendoza's high vineyards, and his daughter Dr Laura Catena now runs the bodega ([Hedonism Wines](https://hedonism.co.uk/product/catena-zapata-malbec-argentino-2018)). Nicolás has been named Decanter's Man of the Year, and Wine Spectator gave him its Distinguished Service Award ([Catena Zapata](https://catenazapata.com/family)).

**The wine: Argentino.** Argentino is the family's flagship Malbec, the Catenas' attempt "to produce an Argentine Malbec that can stand with the great wines of the world". Since 2015 it has come from two historic high-altitude vineyards: Angélica, at 920 metres in Lunlunta, Maipú, and Nicasia, at 1,095 metres in San Carlos in the [Uco Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uco_Valley). Both are picked in two stages and fermented in open barrels, 20% as whole bunches ([Hedonism Wines](https://hedonism.co.uk/product/catena-zapata-malbec-argentino-2018)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Argentina vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/argentina) says low rain and cool temperatures in the February-to-April harvest gave fruit of "optimal ripeness", according to Laura Catena: apparently a classic year for Mendoza Malbec, with smooth tannins and fresh natural acidity, and yields back to normal after the short 2016 and 2017 harvests.

**What the critics say for 2018.**
- **[Vinous](https://vinous.com): 94** (Joaquín Hidalgo, October 2020, as listed by [Hedonism Wines](https://hedonism.co.uk/product/catena-zapata-malbec-argentino-2018)). Dark purple; ripe dark fruit with herbs and fine wood, "a balsamic red with further notes of thyme and violets"; good volume, with gentle tannins in "a classical, nuanced Mendoza Malbec style".
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.7** (from your CellarTracker list).
- (Retail pages also list Wine Advocate and Suckling notes, but without scores I could read, so I've left them out.)

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eight years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2022 to 2029. So it is in its prime: dark plum, violet, thyme and balsamic notes over gentle tannins. Decant an hour ahead and serve at 16 to 18°C.

**Food.** Malbec and grilled beef are made for each other: an Argentine [asado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asado) with [chimichurri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimichurri), skirt steak, beef [empanadas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empanada), or lamb with rosemary.

**Value and where to buy.** Catena is everywhere here. The Argentino itself: BC Liquor has the 2022 at $149.99, BSW Liquor the 2023 at $120, and ZYN the 2023 at $131. Its siblings include Nicolás Catena Zapata (ZYN, 2020 and 2021 from $148.99), Nicasia Malbec ($124.99 at BC Liquor), the Adrianna Vineyard single-plot Malbecs ($169.99 to $405), and the excellent-value Catena Alta and High Mountain Vines ranges from about $23.

**From the history books**
- **A century of family winemaking.** Catena Zapata began with Nicola Catena's first Mendoza vineyard in 1902 ([Hedonism Wines](https://hedonism.co.uk/product/catena-zapata-malbec-argentino-2018)).
- **Malbec's second life.** Catena Zapata is known for its pioneering role in resurrecting Malbec ([Catena Zapata](https://catenazapata.com/family)).

**Curious details**
- **Altitude as a tool.** The Catenas' insight was that high altitude, cooler nights and intense sun could make fresher, more complex Malbec; Adrianna sits at almost 5,000 feet ([Catena Zapata](https://catenazapata.com/family)).
